items.problem: `put_notice` of a stored `notice_id` answers success without storing anything when `sweep_expired` deletes the row between the live check and the `UPDATE`. Run path on PostgreSQL (`READ COMMITTED`): a notice is close to its `end_at`; `put_notice` takes `lock_game_row` and `SELECT_LIVE_ONE` (index.ts:402) sees the row with `end_at` > `clock_now`; the clock reaches `end_at`; `sweep_expired` of any server instance deletes the row, because the `storage` `### expiry` sweep takes no `lock_game_row` lock; `UPDATE_NOTICE` (index.ts:406) then changes 0 rows and its row count is not looked at. The handler returns `{notice_id}`, admin-api writes the `admin_api_operation` row so a retry with the same `operation_id` gets the same success, and `after_commit` puts the replaced notice in the cache of that server instance until the next `notice_cache` run, after which it is gone. An operator who extends a notice as it ends gets success and loses the notice. Found by reading the code path; the window is the gap between two statements, and it was not reproduced in a run. The fix direction is one upsert statement for the replace, or `not_found` when the `UPDATE` changed no row

No core test goes through the `INVALID_REQUEST` failure value that `## API` of `notice` sets for `GetNotices` with `language` over `max_len` 35. Every `GetNoticesRequest` sent in `server/core/notice/tests/`, `server/core/routing/tests/processing-order.test.ts` and `server/core/testing/tests/request.test.ts` has a default or short `language` (longest: `ko-KR`), so removing `max_len` from `proto/ogw/core.proto:1183` fails no test that those files hold
